messages.author: 6d516dae6aab4320
messages.subject: NAMESPACE issues
parts:
Hey all,

I have an R package called "prepdat" available on CRAN  https://cran.r-project.org/package=prepdat and GitHub https://github.com/ayalaallon/prepdat. My package contains the following functions and I want the user to have full access to these functions:
prep()
read_data()
file_merge()
non_recursive_mc()
modified_recursive_mc()
hybrid_recursive_mc()


and this is how the NAMESPACE file looks like


# Generated by roxygen2 (4.1.1): do not edit by hand

export(prep)
export(read_data)
export(file_merge)
export(non_recursive_mc)
export(modified_recursive_mc)
export(hybrid_recursive_mc)
importFrom(dplyr, "%>%")
importFrom("stats", "ave", "median", "quantile", "sd")
importFrom("utils", "head", "read.csv", "read.table", "write.table") 



The problem is that after you install the package and load it using
library(prepdat)
only the prep() function is available and you can access the rest of the functions using ::: (for example prepdat:::file_merge()).

How can I change the NAMESPACE file so all the functions will be available to the user?

Any help will be greatly appreciated.

Best,

Ayala

messages.author: a305e65fa9dfb74d
messages.subject: Re: [Israel RUG] NAMESPACE issues
parts:
I downloaded your package form git, built it, and TADA! No problem...

I thus suggest the following:
Assuming you are working on MS Windows, make sure you have all the windows toolset installed. 
Also make sure you restart R before building and loading the package. (CTRL+Shift+B in RStudio typically does that for you, but a little  CTRL+Shift+F10 before loading can't hurt).

I should also mention that the package failed an R CMD check. Indeed, magrittr does not appear in your DESCRIPTION file.





PS- I am not a big fan of Roxygen....

messages.subject: Re: [Israel RUG] NAMESPACE issues
parts:
Hey Jonathan,

I already installed Rtools33.exe when I was writing the package if this is what you meant.  
As regards to the RCMD check I'm attaching a record of the RCMD check I did before submitting the current version to CRAN. I run my RCMD check using

devtools::check(document = FALSE)

Before submission I used

devtools::build(prepdat)
 to build the package.
In addition I have to note that for this submission I didn't get any comments from the guys on CRAN during the submission process.

Anyway I removed my package, restarted the session and installed it again using install.packages("prepdat") (although I am pretty sure I tried that before asking here) and all my functions are now available.

Thank you!
Ayala
